import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card
import Mathlib.Tactic.Push
import Aesop
set_option maxRecDepth 4096
set_option maxHeartbeats 10000000
namespace Circulant350979
abbrev V := Fin 15
-- A simple path is indexed in order; the iff says precisely that it is induced.
def InducedPath {V : Type} (R : V → V → Prop) (m : ℕ) (f : Fin (m+1) → V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ i j, R (f i) (f j) ↔ i.val + 1 = j.val ∨ j.val + 1 = i.val

def TripleMP {V : Type} (R : V → V → Prop) (a b c : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ m f, InducedPath R m f → ¬ ∃ i j k, f i = a ∧ f j = b ∧ f k = c

lemma triangle_mp {V : Type} {R : V → V → Prop} {a b c : V}
    (ab : R a b) (ac : R a c) (bc : R b c) : TripleMP R a b c := by
  intro m f hp ⟨i,j,k,hi,hj,hk⟩
  have h1 := (hp.2 i j).mp (by simpa [hi,hj] using ab)
  have h2 := (hp.2 i k).mp (by simpa [hi,hk] using ac)
  have h3 := (hp.2 j k).mp (by simpa [hj,hk] using bc)
  omega

lemma twins_mp {V : Type} {R : V → V → Prop} {a b c : V}
    (ab : a ≠ b) (ac : a ≠ c) (bc : b ≠ c)
    (hab : ∀ v, R a v ↔ R b v) (hac : ∀ v, R a v ↔ R c v) : TripleMP R a b c := by
  intro m f hp ⟨i,j,k,hi,hj,hk⟩
  have hij : i.val ≠ j.val := by intro h; have : i=j := Fin.ext h; subst j; exact ab (hi.symm.trans hj)
  have hik : i.val ≠ k.val := by intro h; have : i=k := Fin.ext h; subst k; exact ac (hi.symm.trans hk)
  have hjk : j.val ≠ k.val := by intro h; have : j=k := Fin.ext h; subst k; exact bc (hj.symm.trans hk)
  have hm : 0 < m := by have := i.isLt; have := j.isLt; omega
  have neighbor : ∃ q : Fin (m+1), R a (f q) := by
    by_cases h : i.val < m
    · refine ⟨⟨i.val+1, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      rw [← hi]; exact (hp.2 i _).mpr (Or.inl rfl)
    · refine ⟨⟨i.val-1, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      rw [← hi]; apply (hp.2 i _).mpr; right; dsimp; omega
  obtain ⟨q,hq⟩ := neighbor
  have h1 := (hp.2 i q).mp (by simpa [hi] using hq)
  have h2 := (hp.2 j q).mp (by simpa [hj] using (hab _).mp hq)
  have h3 := (hp.2 k q).mp (by simpa [hk] using (hac _).mp hq)
  omega

-- Bit d selects the cyclic difference ±(d+1), d=0,...,6.
def adj (s : Fin 128) (a b : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ d : Fin 7, s.val.testBit d.val = true ∧
    ((a.val + d.val + 1) % 15 = b.val ∨ (b.val + d.val + 1) % 15 = a.val)
instance (s : Fin 128) (a b : V) : Decidable (adj s a b) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∃ d : Fin 7, s.val.testBit d.val = true ∧ ((a.val+d.val+1)%15=b.val ∨ (b.val+d.val+1)%15=a.val)))

def TriangleFreeAtZero (s : Fin 128) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : V, ¬ (adj s 0 a ∧ adj s 0 b ∧ adj s a b)
def RadiusTwoAtZero (s : Fin 128) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : V, b = 0 ∨ adj s 0 b ∨ ∃ c : V, adj s 0 c ∧ adj s c b
instance (s) : Decidable (TriangleFreeAtZero s) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ a b : V, ¬ (adj s 0 a ∧ adj s 0 b ∧ adj s a b)))
instance (s) : Decidable (RadiusTwoAtZero s) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ b : V, b = 0 ∨ adj s 0 b ∨ ∃ c : V, adj s 0 c ∧ adj s c b))

-- Complete enumeration of all 128 undirected circulants of order 15.
theorem classify : ∀ s : Fin 128,
    TriangleFreeAtZero s → RadiusTwoAtZero s → s = 41 ∨ s = 70 := by decide

theorem twins41 : ∀ v : V, (adj 41 0 v ↔ adj 41 5 v) ∧ (adj 41 0 v ↔ adj 41 10 v) := by decide
theorem twins70 : ∀ v : V, (adj 70 0 v ↔ adj 70 5 v) ∧ (adj 70 0 v ↔ adj 70 10 v) := by decide

theorem obstruction (s : Fin 128) (hd : RadiusTwoAtZero s) :
    ∃ a b c : V, a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c ∧ TripleMP (adj s) a b c := by
  by_cases ht : TriangleFreeAtZero s
  · rcases classify s ht hd with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨0,5,10, by decide, by decide, by decide,
        twins_mp (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (fun v => (twins41 v).1) (fun v => (twins41 v).2)⟩
    · exact ⟨0,5,10, by decide, by decide, by decide,
        twins_mp (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (fun v => (twins70 v).1) (fun v => (twins70 v).2)⟩
  · unfold TriangleFreeAtZero at ht
    push Not at ht
    obtain ⟨a,b,h0a,h0b,hab⟩ := ht
    have hdiag : ∀ v : V, ¬ adj s v v := by
      intro v ⟨d,_,h⟩; rcases h with h | h <;> have := v.isLt <;> have := d.isLt <;> omega
    exact ⟨0,a,b,(by intro h; subst a; exact hdiag 0 h0a),
      (by intro h; subst b; exact hdiag 0 h0b),
      (by intro h; subst b; exact hdiag a hab), triangle_mp h0a h0b hab⟩
end Circulant350979

import Circulant
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Circulant
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
set_option maxRecDepth 8192
set_option maxHeartbeats 10000000
namespace Circulant350979
example (a : V) : ZMod 15 := a

theorem encode : ∀ bits : Fin 7 → Bool, ∃ s : Fin 128,
    ∀ d : Fin 7, s.val.testBit d.val = bits d := by decide

theorem difference_cover : ∀ a b : V, a ≠ b → ∃ d : Fin 7,
    (b : ZMod 15) - a = ((d.val+1 : ℕ) : ZMod 15) ∨ (a : ZMod 15) - b = ((d.val+1 : ℕ) : ZMod 15) := by decide

theorem mod_difference : ∀ a b : V, ∀ d : Fin 7,
    ((a.val+d.val+1)%15=b.val ∨ (b.val+d.val+1)%15=a.val) ↔
    ((b : ZMod 15)-a=((d.val+1 : ℕ) : ZMod 15) ∨ (a : ZMod 15)-b=((d.val+1 : ℕ) : ZMod 15)) := by decide

theorem represent (J : Set (ZMod 15)) : ∃ s : Fin 128,
    ∀ a b : V, (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J).Adj a b ↔ adj s a b := by
  classical
  let G := SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J
  obtain ⟨s,hs⟩ := encode (fun d => decide (G.Adj 0 (d.val+1 : ℕ)))
  refine ⟨s,?_⟩
  intro a b
  have h0 : ∀ x y : ZMod 15, G.Adj x y ↔ G.Adj 0 (y-x) := by
    intro x y
    have h := SimpleGraph.circulantGraph_adj_translate (s:=J) (u:=0) (v:=y-x) (d:=x)
    change G.Adj (0+x) ((y-x)+x) ↔ G.Adj 0 (y-x) at h
    simpa only [zero_add, sub_add_cancel] using h
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨d,hd⟩ := difference_cover a b (G.ne_of_adj h)
    refine ⟨d,?_,(mod_difference a b d).mpr hd⟩
    rw [hs]; apply decide_eq_true
    rcases hd with hd | hd
    · exact hd ▸ (h0 a b).mp h
    · exact hd ▸ (h0 b a).mp h.symm
  · rintro ⟨d,hd,hab⟩
    have h : G.Adj 0 (d.val+1 : ℕ) := of_decide_eq_true (by simpa [hs] using hd)
    rcases (mod_difference a b d).mp hab with hab | hab
    · exact (h0 a b).mpr (hab.symm ▸ h)
    · exact ((h0 b a).mpr (hab.symm ▸ h)).symm
end Circulant350979
files.formal/Endpoint.lean:
import Bridge
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Diam
set_option maxRecDepth 8192
set_option maxHeartbeats 10000000
namespace Circulant350979

def MonophonicSet {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, ∀ c ∈ S, a ≠ b → a ≠ c → b ≠ c → TripleMP R a b c

noncomputable def mpNumber {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (MonophonicSet G.Adj)).sup Finset.card

lemma mp_triple {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] {R : α → α → Prop} {a b c : α}
    (h : TripleMP R a b c) : MonophonicSet R {a,b,c} := by
  intro x hx y hy z hz hxy hxz hyz m f hp hxyz
  obtain ⟨i,j,k,hi,hj,hk⟩ := hxyz
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy hz
  apply h m f hp
  rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hz with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> aesop

lemma lower_bound (G : SimpleGraph V) (a b c : V)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbc : b ≠ c) (h : TripleMP G.Adj a b c) :
    3 ≤ mpNumber G := by
  classical
  have hm : {a,b,c} ∈ Finset.univ.filter (MonophonicSet G.Adj) := by
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]; exact mp_triple h
  have hc : ({a,b,c} : Finset V).card = 3 := by simp [hab,hac,hbc]
  simpa only [mpNumber,hc] using (Finset.le_sup (f:=Finset.card) hm)

lemma radius_of_diam (G : SimpleGraph V) (hd : G.diam = 2) :
    ∀ b : V, b=0 ∨ G.Adj 0 b ∨ ∃ c : V, G.Adj 0 c ∧ G.Adj c b := by
  intro b
  have htop := G.ediam_ne_top_of_diam_ne_zero (by omega)
  have hdist := G.dist_le_diam htop (u:=0) (v:=b)
  rw [hd] at hdist
  have he : G.edist 0 b = (G.dist 0 b : ℕ∞) := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.dist]; exact (ENat.natCast_toNat (ne_top_of_le_ne_top htop G.edist_le_ediam)).symm
  have hcases : G.dist 0 b = 0 ∨ G.dist 0 b = 1 ∨ G.dist 0 b = 2 := by omega
  rcases hcases with h | h | h
  · left; have : G.edist 0 b = 0 := by simpa [h] using he
    exact (G.edist_eq_zero_iff.mp this).symm
  · right; left; exact G.edist_eq_one_iff_adj.mp (by simpa [h] using he)
  · right; right
    obtain ⟨c,hc⟩ := (G.edist_eq_two_iff.mp (by simpa [h] using he)).2.2
    exact ⟨c,hc.1,hc.2.symm⟩

theorem order15 (J : Set (ZMod 15))
    (hd : (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J).diam = 2) :
    3 ≤ mpNumber (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J) := by
  obtain ⟨s,hs⟩ := represent J
  have hr : RadiusTwoAtZero s := by
    intro b
    rcases radius_of_diam (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J) hd b with h | h | ⟨c,hc,hb⟩
    · exact Or.inl h
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ((hs 0 b).mp h))
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨c,(hs 0 c).mp hc,(hs c b).mp hb⟩)
  obtain ⟨a,b,c,hab,hac,hbc,hmp⟩ := obstruction s hr
  apply lower_bound (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J) a b c hab hac hbc
  intro m f hp
  apply hmp m f
  exact ⟨hp.1,fun i j => (hs (f i) (f j)).symm.trans (hp.2 i j)⟩

-- Source Conjecture 4.5, with actual circulant graphs, diameter and maximum
-- cardinality of a set containing no three vertices of an induced path.
def SourceClaim : Prop := ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 11 ≤ n),
  letI : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  ∃ J : Set (ZMod n),
  (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J).diam = 2 ∧ mpNumber (SimpleGraph.circulantGraph J) = 2

theorem source_refutation : ¬ SourceClaim := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨J,hd,hm⟩ := h 15 (by omega)
  have := order15 J hd
  omega
end Circulant350979
files.formal/Audit.lean:
import Endpoint
import Lean
open Lean Elab Command
set_option pp.all true
run_cmd do
  let env ← getEnv
  let mut count : Nat := 0
  for (n,c) in env.constants.toList do
    let some idx := env.getModuleIdxFor? n | continue
    let m := env.header.moduleNames[idx.toNat]!
    if (["Circulant", "Bridge", "Endpoint"] : List String).contains m.toString then
      count := count + 1
      let ax ← Lean.collectAxioms n
      logInfo m!"DECL|{n}|MODULE|{m}|UNSAFE|{c.isUnsafe}|PARTIAL|{c.isPartial}|AXIOMS|{ax.toList}"
      if c.isUnsafe || c.isPartial then throwError "bad safety {n}"
      match c with
      | .axiomInfo _ => throwError "local axiom {n}"
      | _ => pure ()
      match c with
      | .inductInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|inductive|{n}"
      | .ctorInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|constructor|{n}"
      | .recInfo _ => logInfo m!"KERNEL_DECL_KIND|recursor|{n}"
      | _ => if !(c.value? true).isSome then throwError "missing body {n}"
      for x in ax do
        if !([``propext, ``Classical.choice, ``Quot.sound] : List Name).contains x then
          throwError "disallowed axiom {x} in {n}"
  logInfo m!"AUDITED_LOCAL_DECLARATIONS|{count}"

#print axioms Circulant350979.source_refutation
#print axioms Circulant350979.order15

"""Independent modular classification and positive-witness verification. No writes."""
from pathlib import Path
import json,itertools
W=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
counts={'triangle':0,'distance_obstruction':0,'residual':0}
res=[]
for m in range(128):
 S={v%15 for d in range(1,8) if m>>(d-1)&1 for v in [d,-d]}
 if any((b-a)%15 in S for a in S for b in S):label='triangle'
 elif len({0}|S|{(a+b)%15 for a in S for b in S})<15:label='distance_obstruction'
 else:label='residual';res.append(m)
 counts[label]+=1
 row=json.loads((W/'evidence/classification.json').read_text())['rows'][m]
 assert row['mask']==m and row['label']==label
assert counts=={'triangle':109,'distance_obstruction':17,'residual':2} and res==[41,70]
rows=json.loads((W/'evidence/coverage-verified.json').read_text())
assert [r['n'] for r in rows]==list(range(11,41))
for row in rows:
 n=row['n']
 if n==15:assert not row['exists'];continue
 assert row['exists'];r=row['certificate'];assert r['n']==n
 S={x%n for d in r['positive_jumps'] for x in [d,-d]};covered=set()
 for p in r['witnesses'].values():
  assert len(p)==len(set(p)) and all(0<=v<n for v in p)
  assert all((((b-a)%n in S)==(j==i+1)) for i,a in enumerate(p) for j,b in enumerate(p) if i<j)
  for delta in range(n):
   for t in itertools.combinations(p,3):covered.add(tuple(sorted((x+delta)%n for x in t)))
 assert len(covered)==n*(n-1)*(n-2)//6
 assert len({0}|S|{(a+b)%n for a in S for b in S})==n and len(S)<n-1
print('PASS: 128 masks (109/17/2); all triple-path witnesses at 29 orders in 11..40 except 15')

"""Extract a bounded source archive into a NEW directory, refusing unsafe names."""
from pathlib import Path,PurePosixPath
import sys,zipfile,stat,json,hashlib
archive=Path(sys.argv[1]);dest=Path(sys.argv[2]);assert not dest.exists(),'destination exists'
with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as z:
 infos=z.infolist();assert len(infos)<100 and len({i.filename for i in infos})==len(infos)
 assert sum(i.file_size for i in infos)<8*1024**2
 for i in infos:
  p=PurePosixPath(i.filename)
  assert not p.is_absolute() and '..' not in p.parts and '\\' not in i.filename
  assert not stat.S_ISLNK(i.external_attr>>16) and not i.is_dir()
  assert not any(x.endswith(('.olean','.ilean','.so','.pyc')) for x in p.parts)
 dest.mkdir(parents=True)
 for i in infos:
  out=dest/i.filename;out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);out.write_bytes(z.read(i))
print(json.dumps({'status':'PASS','archive_sha256':hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'files':len(infos),'destination':str(dest)}))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fresh sequential replay. All outputs remain in the extraction."""
from pathlib import Path
import os, sys, json, subprocess, hashlib, resource, time, signal, re
W=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
os.chdir(W)
if any(W.rglob('*.olean*')):sys.exit('REFUSED: existing oleans')
for d in ['logs','receipts','tmp']:(W/d).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
B=Path(os.environ['LEAN_BIN']).resolve(); P=Path(os.environ['LEAN_PACKAGES']).resolve()
env=os.environ.copy()
for k in ['LEAN_PATH','LEAN_SRC_PATH','LEAN_PLUGIN_PATH','LD_PRELOAD','LEAN_OPTS']:env.pop(k,None)
env.update(LEAN_PATH=':'.join([str(W/'formal')]+[str(p/'.lake/build/lib/lean') for p in sorted(P.iterdir()) if (p/'.lake/build/lib/lean').is_dir()]),PATH=str(B)+':'+env['PATH'],MALLOC_ARENA_MAX='2',LEAN_NUM_THREADS='1',TMPDIR=str(W/'tmp'),PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
def limits():
 os.sched_setaffinity(0,sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(0))[:2]);resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU,(120,120))
def run(label,cmd,expected=0):
 start=time.monotonic();peak=0;killed=None
 with (W/'logs'/f'{label}.log').open('w') as f:
  p=subprocess.Popen(cmd,env=env,stdout=f,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,start_new_session=True,preexec_fn=limits)
  while p.poll() is None:
   # Sum resident memory of the process group, counting shared pages conservatively.
   rss=0
   for proc in Path('/proc').iterdir():
    if not proc.name.isdigit():continue
    try:
     if os.getpgid(int(proc.name)) != p.pid:continue
     for line in (proc/'status').read_text().splitlines():
      if line.startswith('VmRSS:'):rss+=int(line.split()[1])
    except (OSError,ValueError,ProcessLookupError):pass
   peak=max(peak,rss)
   if rss>6*1024*1024 or time.monotonic()-start>140:
    killed='RSS or wall cap';os.killpg(p.pid,signal.SIGKILL);break
   time.sleep(.1)
  p.wait()
 r=dict(command=list(map(str,cmd)),returncode=p.returncode,seconds=time.monotonic()-start,peak_RSS_KiB=peak,killed=killed,cpu_limit_s=120,wall_limit_s=140,affinity_cpus=2)
 (W/'receipts'/f'{label}.json').write_text(json.dumps(r,indent=2)+'\n')
 if p.returncode!=expected or killed:raise RuntimeError(label+' failed; see logs')
 return r
for file,h in json.loads((W/'SOURCE-MANIFEST.json').read_text()).items():
 assert hashlib.sha256((W/file).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==h,file
run('version',[str(B/'lean'),'--version'])
v=(W/'logs/version.log').read_text();assert '4.34.1' in v and '5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52' in v
run('certificates',[sys.executable,'-I',str(W/'scripts/verify_certificates.py')])
for m in ['Circulant','Bridge','Endpoint','Audit','AuditFull','Control16','NegativeMutation']:
 text=(W/'formal'/f'{m}.lean').read_text()
 if m not in ['Audit','AuditFull']:assert not re.search(r'\b(sorry|admit|axiom|unsafe|partial|native_decide|ofReduceBool|implemented_by|extern)\b',text),m
 run('build-'+m,[str(B/'lean'),'-j1','-DwarningAsError=true',f'formal/{m}.lean','-o',f'formal/{m}.olean'])
 # Exactly one module per checker process.
 run('check-'+m,[str(B/'leanchecker'),m])
s=(W/'logs/build-AuditFull.log').read_text()
assert 'AUDITED_LOCAL_DECLARATIONS|52' in s
assert s.count('TYPE|')==52 and s.count('BODY|')==52 and s.count('DECL|')==52
for m in ['FalseClassification','FalseOrder16']:
 run('negative-'+m,[str(B/'lean'),'-j1','-DwarningAsError=true',f'negative/{m}.lean'],1)
 s=(W/'logs'/f'negative-{m}.log').read_text()
 assert 'error:' in s and ('false' in s or 'not true' in s),m

assert p.returncode!=0 and 'REFUSED: existing oleans' in p.stderr

# Reproduction

This is a draft dossier for MathDB 350979. Acceptance credit is zero. Run from an extracted source-only archive. Python 3, Linux /proc, the pinned Lean binaries and the pinned mathlib package cache are required. No network is used during replay.

```bash
python3 -I scripts/extract_safe.py circulant-source-only.zip fresh-copy
cd fresh-copy
export LEAN_BIN=/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/dlp-research/.tools/lean-4.34.1-linux/bin
export LEAN_PACKAGES=/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research/frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/formal/.lake/packages
python3 -I replay.py
```

The source archive contains its own safe extractor as well; use the dossier's script for the initial extraction. Choose a new extraction directory on every attempt. The driver refuses any existing local olean, validates SOURCE-MANIFEST.json, and checks the exact Lean version and commit. The mathlib revision is d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612; provide that cache through LEAN_PACKAGES. This is a dependency pin, not an independent rebuild or semantic validation of all upstream modules.

Every heavy child runs sequentially with at most two CPU cores, RLIMIT_CPU 120 seconds, a 140-second wall watchdog, sampled aggregate process-group RSS at most 6 GiB, and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2. Child output goes to logs/ and receipts to receipts/. RSS monitoring samples shared pages conservatively and is not a transient-peak guarantee. No child is intentionally left running.

The driver independently checks all 128 classification cases and all positive coverage witnesses, builds Circulant, Bridge, Endpoint, Audit, AuditFull and the two positive controls, and checks each module in a separate leanchecker process. Never combine checker module arguments: the review's combined attempt exceeded its RSS cap. All Lean builds use -j1 -DwarningAsError=true. AuditFull prints all 52 local declaration types, opaque bodies, flags and transitive axioms. Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed. The positive order-16 control contains 560 paths. The mutation negation is a positive control. Both files in negative/ must fail with a false-decision diagnostic; nonzero status caused by a resource limit or missing import is not a pass. A repeated replay must refuse stale oleans.

The original four modules have byte identity recorded in MODULE-HASHES.json. The original supplied ZIP and its mandated SHA-256 are retained in evidence/. The exact MathDB raw line and its SHA-256 are in sources/. Original source bodies, access receipts and review evidence are retained in the full dossier; SOURCE-MANIFEST.json covers source-replay inputs. The source-only ZIP omits generated local oleans, replay outputs and bulky source bodies. files.PROOF.md:
# Ordinary proof and source correspondence

1. The question and its scope

Abstract. We give a finite, kernel-checked refutation of Conjecture 4.5 of Tuite, Thomas and Chandran. Every circulant graph on 15 vertices with diameter 2 has monophonic position number at least 3. Among its 128 possible undirected jump masks, 109 contain a triangle, 17 further masks fail the distance bound, and the remaining two describe the same C5 blow-up, whose independent fibers contain triples of twins. The exact monophonic position number of that familiar residual graph is 6. The accompanying Lean dossier proves the literal negation of the source conjecture; the finite computation is part of the proof.

All graphs here are finite, simple and undirected. A monophonic path is an induced path: a sequence of distinct vertices in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when their indices are consecutive. A monophonic position set (mp-set) contains no three distinct vertices on a common induced path. Its maximum cardinality is the monophonic position number mp(G). Equivalently, no member of the set lies internally on an induced path between two other members. Indeed, from three selected vertices on a common path, take the subpath from the first to the last. Conversely, a violation of the internal-vertex condition supplies three members on one induced path. This condition concerns all induced paths, of arbitrary length.

For J contained in {1,...,floor(n/2)}, write C_n(J) for the graph on Z/n with edges of differences plus or minus a member of J. This represents every circulant up to cyclic labelling. A general Cayley generating set gives the same simple undirected graph after symmetrization and removal of zero. The conjecture is existential in J for each order n; it does not assert the property for every J.

Source context [1]. Lemma 4.3 states: if a graph of order r >= 4 has mp-number 2 and diameter 2, then such graphs also exist at orders 3r, 3r+1 and 3r+2. Theorem 4.4 states that a graph of order n with mp-number 2 and diameter 2 exists if and only if n is in {3,4,5,8} or n >= 11. Its proof uses computer search for n <= 32 and then Lemma 4.3 inductively. These statements concern unrestricted graphs. The search is credited to Erskine by personal communication; the underlying data are not printed.

Conjecture 4.5 [1] strengthens the large-order assertion: for every n >= 11, there exists a circulant graph of order n with diameter 2 and mp-number 2. The survey [3], cached v5 dated 16 August 2026, repeats it in Section 4.1 and asks for its proof in the open-problem list. We refute precisely this assertion at the interior order 15. Theorem 4.4 and its unrestricted construction are unaffected.

2. Two obstructions and the finite classification

Lemma 1 (triangles). The vertices of a triangle form an mp-set. Proof. If three pairwise adjacent vertices lay on an induced path, their three distinct indices would have to be pairwise consecutive. Three distinct integers cannot have this property. Thus mp(G) >= 3 whenever G contains a triangle.

Lemma 2 (open twins). Three distinct vertices a, b, c with N(a) = N(b) = N(c) form an mp-set. Proof. Equality of open neighborhoods implies that these vertices are pairwise nonadjacent: adjacency of a and b would put b in its own neighborhood. If an induced path contained all three, it would have positive length, and a would have a neighbor q on that path. Equality of neighborhoods makes q adjacent to b and c as well. It is different from all three. The induced subgraph of a path has degree at most 2, whereas q would have three distinct neighbors. This is impossible.

Classification lemma. A triangle-free circulant on 15 vertices for which every vertex is at distance at most 2 from zero has positive jumps {1,4,6} or {2,3,7}. Here is the complete finite certificate, together with its elementary decision rule. Encode J by m = sum of 2^(d-1) over d in J, so 0 <= m < 128. Put S = J union (-J) in Z/15. A triangle through zero exists exactly when a,b are in S and b-a is in S. By translation, absence of such a triangle is triangle-freeness of the whole graph. Two-step reachability from zero is exactly {0} union S union (S+S).

The following table lists every mask passing the triangle test. The second row supplies a vertex outside {0} union S union (S+S), or a dash when there is none. The other 109 masks fail the triangle test. Each entry can be checked with residues 0 through 14; no graph-isomorphism algorithm or numerical tolerance enters.

Masks: 0 1 2 4 5 6 8 9 12 32 33 34 40 41 64 66 68 70 96
Missing: 1 3 1 1 5 7 1 6 2 1 4 1 1 - 2 3 2 - 4

For completeness, the exhaustive rule is: for m = 0,...,127 form S; if some a,b in S have b-a in S, record triangle; otherwise test each x = 0,...,14 for x in {0} union S union (S+S). The table gives all 19 masks surviving the first test; exactly 17 fail the second. Lean's theorem classify proves the universal implication over Fin 128 by decidable reduction in the kernel. The independent Python certificate uses the displayed modular rule. The human-readable table and executable rule specify the entire finite calculation, rather than an unexplained search for examples.

The survivors have masks 41 = 1+8+32 and 70 = 2+4+64. Multiplication by 2 modulo 15 sends the signed jumps of {1,4,6} to those of {2,3,7}; it is a graph isomorphism.

3. Refutation and the residual structure

Theorem. For every circulant G of order 15 with diameter 2, mp(G) >= 3. In particular, Conjecture 4.5 of [1] is false.

Proof. If G has a triangle, apply Lemma 1. Otherwise label its vertices by Z/15 and let J be its positive jumps. Diameter 2 implies that every vertex is reachable from zero in at most two steps, so the classification lemma gives J = {1,4,6} or J = {2,3,7}. In the first case the full signed jump set is the six residues congruent to plus or minus 1 modulo 5; in the second it is the six residues congruent to plus or minus 2 modulo 5. Consequently 0, 5 and 10 have identical open neighborhoods. Lemma 2 gives a three-element mp-set. Hence no jump set at n = 15 can satisfy both diameter 2 and mp-number 2. Since 15 >= 11, the universal existential statement in the conjecture is false.

The five cosets of {0,5,10} are independent fibers of size 3. Between two fibers all edges or no edges occur, and the quotient is C5 (with quotient step 1 or step 2). Thus each residual graph is the lexicographic product C5[3K1]. It has diameter 2: adjacent quotient fibers are joined completely, two nonadjacent quotient fibers have an intermediate fiber, and two vertices in one fiber have a common neighbor.

Remark (known exact value). In fact mp(C5[3K1]) = 6. For a direct check, any three distinct vertices of C5 lie on an induced path: delete a suitable one of the two unselected cycle vertices, leaving an induced four-vertex path. Prescribed members of three distinct fibers can therefore be lifted onto an induced path, so an mp-set meets at most two fibers and has size at most 6. For the lower bound take all vertices of two nonadjacent fibers. If an induced path contains two vertices from one fiber, their identical neighborhoods force them to be the two ends of a path of length 2: any extension creates a chord. Such a path cannot also meet the chosen nonadjacent fiber. Therefore no three members of this six-element set lie on an induced path.

This exact value receives no separate novelty claim. The lexicographic-product formula in [4, Theorem 4.4] already gives it. For a connected base G of order at least 2 that formula maximizes n_M omega(H) + r_M mp(H) over mp-sets M of G, where r_M counts isolated vertices of G[M] and n_M counts vertices in its nontrivial components. For H = 3K1, omega(H) = 1 and mp(H) = 3. A nonadjacent pair in C5 contributes 6; every base mp-set has at most two vertices. The formula thus gives the same value.

Coverage and corrected question. The review dossier verifies explicit circulant witnesses at every order 11 through 40 except 15. Each witness has two-step reachability, a missing edge, and induced paths containing every triple of vertices; hence diameter is exactly 2 and mp-number is exactly 2 (any pair is an mp-set). At 15 the exclusion is exhaustive over all masks. Positive witnesses at the other orders do not classify all masks. Does such a circulant exist for every n >= 11 with n != 15? This natural corrected question remains OPEN here. No assertion is made above order 40.

4. Formal statement correspondence and replay

The namespace below is Circulant350979; module names are Circulant, Bridge and Endpoint. The four supplied modules, including Audit, are byte-identical to expanded-corpus-r108. AuditFull is a new full declaration audit adapted from the independent review. The correspondence is as follows.

Mathlib's circulantGraph J is fromRel of the difference relation. It symmetrizes that relation and removes loops; arbitrary asymmetric J and J containing zero introduce no extra graphs. Bridge.represent therefore covers every circulant at order 15. Fin 15 and ZMod 15 use the compatible finite residue representation in this development.

Mathlib defines the natural diameter of a disconnected graph as 0. The hypothesis diam = 2 excludes this case: radius_of_diam first proves the extended diameter is finite, then bounds distances. Thus neither disconnected graphs nor a diameter convention creates a spurious refutation. The source quantifier uses natural orders; under n >= 11 this agrees with integer orders.

The dossier pins Lean 4.34.1, commit 5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52, and mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612. The replay driver accepts LEAN_BIN and LEAN_PACKAGES, rejects existing local oleans, verifies source hashes, and builds sequentially with -j1 and warningAsError. It then runs leanchecker with exactly one module per process. Each child has at most two CPUs, a 120-second CPU limit, a 140-second wall watchdog and a sampled aggregate RSS limit of 6 GiB; MALLOC_ARENA_MAX is 2.

AuditFull enumerates all 52 declarations originating in the three proof modules, including generated declarations, and prints their full types, bodies using value? (allowOpaque := true), safety flags and transitive axioms. It rejects local axioms, missing ordinary bodies, unsafe or partial declarations, and any axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Two deliberately false Lean claims must be rejected: substituting mask 40 for 41, and denying triple-path coverage at the positive order-16 control.

Trust limits. Decidable finite reduction is kernel-checked; no native_decide, ofReduceBool, sorry, admit or added axiom is used. The Lean implementation, allowed logical axioms, operating system, binary and cached upstream mathlib oleans remain trusted. Mathlib is pinned but not rebuilt. Leanchecker rechecks exported environments using the same kernel implementation; it is not a second foundational implementation. RSS sampling does not certify every transient peak. The exact residual mp-number and coverage through 40 are supplementary ordinary/executable results, not additional theorems claimed by the source_refutation endpoint.

5. Related work, access limits and references

The monophonic-position precursor [2] develops the invariant and standard clique and structural bounds. Its Lemma 3.1 describes the induced structure of an mp-set as a disjoint union of cliques. These observations and the source's own blow-up arguments explain the residual obstruction; the additional finite step here excludes every other order-15 circulant. The product theorem [4] subsumes the exact residual value. No priority is claimed for that value, the twin mechanism, or the underlying graph.

The graph-likelihood paper [5, Section 6] explicitly uses the same 15-vertex circulant C5[3K1] in a different extremal problem. That graph is therefore familiar. A likelihood counterexample does not establish the universal exclusion for the monophonic-position conjecture; conversely, this manuscript makes no graph-likelihood claim.

Access and novelty limits. This draft reads the retained arXiv bodies selectively, concentrating on the definitions and relevant theorem sections. The journal version of [1] is reported as Ars Mathematica Contemporanea (2025), but its actual body was not read: the retained access receipt records HTTP 403. No access barrier was retried. The journal is not silently treated as equivalent to the read preprint. The independent review found no earlier exact refutation in its bounded searches and retained registry screens; it did not clear all citing literature or semantically inspect every public proof. Its qualified finding and the root's conditional eligibility ruling are included in the dossier. This manuscript asserts no worldwide priority and assigns zero campaign acceptance credit.

The following bibliography identifies the bodies actually used in this manuscript, rather than uninspected search snippets or the unread journal body. Retrieval receipts, original bodies and their hashes are retained under sources/. Version metadata are copied from those retained bodies and receipts; no new live literature survey was performed for this packaging task.

[1] James Tuite, Elias John Thomas and Ullas Chandran S. V. On some extremal position problems for graphs. arXiv:2106.06827v3, 8 February 2022. Read: definitions, Lemma 4.3, Theorem 4.4 and Conjecture 4.5. https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06827v3 . Journal body (Ars Mathematica Contemporanea, 2025) unread; 403 receipt retained.

[2] Elias John Thomas, Ullas Chandran S. V., James Tuite and Gabriele Di Stefano. On monophonic position sets in graphs. arXiv:2012.10330, retained HTML body. Read: definitions and Lemma 3.1 with its proof. https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10330 .

[3] Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavzar and James Tuite. The General Position Problem: A Survey. arXiv:2501.19385v5, 16 August 2026. Read: Section 4.1 and the relevant Section 6 open problem. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19385v5 .

[4] Ullas Chandran S. V., Sandi Klavzar, Neethu P. K. and James Tuite. Monophonic position sets of Cartesian and lexicographic products of graphs. arXiv:2412.09837v3 (version header: 17 November 2025; body dateline: 24 August 2026). Read: Section 4, especially Theorem 4.4 and its proof. https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09837v3 .

[5] Simone Severini and Eric W. Weisstein. The minimum of the graph likelihood. arXiv:2608.19467v2, 29 October 2026. Read selectively: Section 6 and the C5 blow-up description. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19467v2 .

from pathlib import Path
import json,html
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate,Paragraph,Spacer,PageBreak,Table,TableStyle
from reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle
from reportlab.lib import colors
W=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
body=ParagraphStyle('body',fontName='Times-Roman',fontSize=10.5,leading=13.1,spaceAfter=8)
small=ParagraphStyle('small',parent=body,fontSize=9,leading=11,spaceAfter=6)
head=ParagraphStyle('head',parent=body,fontName='Times-Bold',fontSize=14,leading=17,spaceAfter=12)
title=ParagraphStyle('title',parent=head,fontSize=19,leading=22)
def p(s,style=body):return Paragraph(html.escape(s),style)
def table(rows,widths):
 t=Table([[p(str(x),small) for x in row] for row in rows],colWidths=widths,hAlign='LEFT')
 t.setStyle(TableStyle([('VALIGN',(0,0),(-1,-1),'TOP'),('BACKGROUND',(0,0),(-1,0),colors.HexColor('#eaf0f5')),('LINEBELOW',(0,0),(-1,0),.5,colors.grey),('LEFTPADDING',(0,0),(-1,-1),6),('RIGHTPADDING',(0,0),(-1,-1),6),('BOTTOMPADDING',(0,0),(-1,-1),5)]));return t
story=[]
for i,page in enumerate(json.loads((W/'manuscript.json').read_text())):
 if i:story.append(PageBreak())
 if 'title' in page:story += [p(page['title'],title),p(page['subtitle'],small),Spacer(1,8)]
 story.append(p(page['heading'],head))
 story += [p(x) for x in page['paragraphs']]
 if page.get('table')=='classification':
  story += [table([['Mask m','Missing vertex'],['0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12','1, 3, 1, 1, 5, 7, 1, 6, 2'],['32, 33, 34, 40, 41','1, 4, 1, 1, -'],['64, 66, 68, 70, 96','2, 3, 2, -, 4']],[260,235]),Spacer(1,10)]
 if page.get('table')=='correspondence':
  rows=[['Declaration','Mathematical content'],['InducedPath R m f','Injective f on Fin (m+1); adjacency iff consecutive indices.'],['TripleMP R a b c','No induced path contains all three specified vertices.'],['MonophonicSet R S','Every distinct triple of S satisfies TripleMP.'],['mpNumber G','Maximum mp-set cardinality, as a finite supremum.'],['SourceClaim','For every n >= 11 there EXISTS J with diameter 2 and mp-number 2.'],['Bridge.represent (represent)','Every mathlib circulant at order 15 has one of the 128 masks.'],['radius_of_diam','diam = 2 implies every vertex is within two steps of zero.'],['order15','For every J, diam = 2 implies 3 <= mpNumber.'],['source_refutation','The literal negation of SourceClaim, using n = 15.']]
  story += [table(rows,[162,333]),Spacer(1,10)]
 story += [p(x) for x in page.get('after',[])]
 story += [p(x,small) for x in page.get('references',[])]
def footer(c,d):
 c.setFont('Times-Roman',9);c.setFillColor(colors.grey);c.drawString(50,29,'DRAFT | MathDB 350979 | AI-assisted');c.drawRightString(545,29,str(d.page))
doc=SimpleDocTemplate(str(W/'circulant-draft.pdf'),pagesize=(595.28,841.89),leftMargin=50,rightMargin=50,topMargin=42,bottomMargin=45)
doc.build(story,onFirstPage=footer,onLaterPages=footer)
